# FDG9106

> DO place query extensions methods in a “Linq” subnamespace of the main namespace. For example, extension methods for `System.Data` features reside in `System.Data.Linq` namespace.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.6.5 Supporting LINQ through the Query Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9106
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Place the query extension method '{0}' in a Linq subnamespace instead of '{1}'

Library only: the text is about where the users of a feature find its query extensions (System.Data.Linq for System.Data). The text has no body. FDG9106 reports an externally visible extension method named after a method of the Query Pattern that takes a delegate (as for FDG9100) whose namespace does not end in a segment named Linq; the global namespace is reported too. Query extension methods with other names, such as Take or Count, are not checked, and neither is whether the namespace is a subnamespace of the main namespace of the feature, so coverage is partial. Moving a method to another namespace changes the full name of its type for callers, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.
